title: Tee channel
hints: One goroutine does all the work and closes both outputs on its way out (`defer close(out1)`, `defer close(out2)`). Its outer loop is a `select` on `ctx.Done()` and a comma-ok receive from `in`.

Sending `out1 <- v` then `out2 <- v` deadlocks if the reader wants `out2` first. Instead copy the channels into locals `o1, o2 := out1, out2` and loop `for o1 != nil || o2 != nil` with a `select` over both sends; after a send succeeds, set that local to `nil` so its case is disabled.

Inner loop: `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return; case o1 <- v: o1 = nil; case o2 <- v: o2 = nil }`. Outer: `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return; case x, ok := <-in: if !ok { return }; v = x }`. Make both channels with `make(chan T)` and return them as `(out1, out2)`.
